title: The terminal and the dashboard say the name too
name: The terminal and the dashboard say the
description:
The MCP server is one of three surfaces that print a node id, and a name that only the plugin shows is a name that makes the three disagree.

The terminal: packages/cli/src/queue.ts:22 and packages/cli/src/distribute.ts:70 both join bare ids into a sentence, packages/cli/src/hook.ts:158 prints `<id> (waiting on …)` in the message that denies a spawn — which is the one a person reads while being stopped, and therefore the one that most needs to say what was stopped — and packages/cli/src/sync.ts:25 lists ids through `named()`. Check `status.ts` and `board.ts` for the same shape before assuming that list is complete.

The dashboard: check what the canvas and the panel show today before changing anything. If a node already renders its title on the canvas, the name may belong only where space is short — a label under a circle, a chip in a list — and not everywhere at once. Read apps/dashboard/src/canvas/paint.ts and apps/dashboard/src/panel/Panel.tsx first and say in the brief what you found; do not add a second label beside a title that is already legible.

Use the same form the MCP surface uses. Two vocabularies for one board is the thing packages/cli/src/work.ts and apps/dashboard/src/logs/data.ts already argue against for the log marks, and it is the same argument here.

brief.approach: Use the already answered decision: add one node-id/name formatter in packages/cli/src/out.ts, accepting the node record or board so call sites do not hand-build labels. Update bare-id output in packages/cli/src/queue.ts (including drain and held lines), distribute.ts, hook.ts, status.ts and board.ts; keep packages/cli/src/sync.ts's path-specific named() behavior for record paths, but use the formatter for any node ids it prints. Fetch/pass the board where these call sites currently hold only ids. On the dashboard, apps/dashboard/src/canvas/graph.ts already puts node.title in data(label) and paint.ts renders that label, so do not add a second canvas label. In apps/dashboard/src/panel/Panel.tsx show the short name beside the id in the existing metadata row, keeping title as the primary heading. Add focused CLI output tests and a panel render test for the new label; do not touch graph layout or node correction behavior.

acceptance.run: pnpm exec vitest run packages/cli/src/queue.test.ts apps/dashboard/src/panel/Panel.test.tsx
acceptance.proves: Queue wording and the panel show each short name consistently.

acceptance.run: pnpm exec vitest run --project integration test/integration/cli.test.ts
acceptance.proves: The CLI's end-user messages render names with ids in real command flows.

acceptance.run: pnpm exec biome check packages/cli/src/out.ts packages/cli/src/queue.ts packages/cli/src/distribute.ts packages/cli/src/hook.ts packages/cli/src/status.ts packages/cli/src/board.ts apps/dashboard/src/panel/Panel.tsx && pnpm build
acceptance.proves: Changed CLI and dashboard code passes style checks and builds.

plain.what: Show each node's short name with its id in terminal messages and the dashboard panel.
plain.why: The plugin already uses names; terminal and dashboard readers need the same vocabulary.
plain.check: Run focused queue, panel and CLI integration tests, then style and build checks.
plain.risk: Longer terminal lines need to stay readable; the canvas keeps its existing title label.
